name: VeLVET
question: Is fractional CO₂ vaginal laser noninferior to vaginal estrogen cream for menopausal vaginal dryness at six months?

design.population: Menopausal women with bothersome vaginal dryness at six US centers.
design.locator: Publisher full text, Methods and Results, opening paragraph; arm allocation conflicts with registry

verdictNote: Early closure prevented the prespecified noninferiority conclusion.
takeaway: VeLVET compared fractional CO₂ vaginal laser with vaginal conjugated estrogen cream for menopausal vaginal dryness. Both groups improved at six months, but early closure left the trial unable to establish prespecified noninferiority of laser.

reports.label: Six-month primary report
reports.citation: Paraiso MFR, Ferrando CA, Sokol ER, et al. "A randomized clinical trial comparing vaginal laser therapy to vaginal estrogen therapy in women with genitourinary syndrome of menopause: The VeLVET Trial." *Menopause.* 2020;27(1):50-56. doi:10.1097/GME.0000000000001416
reports.followUpLocator: Publisher full text, Methods, outcome measures; Results

results.measure: Vaginal dryness score on a 10-cm VAS at six months; prespecified noninferiority margin 1.0 cm
results.note: The narrative reports no between-group difference and states noninferiority could not be established after early closure. The numerical primary comparison is in an image table unavailable as text.
results.locator: Publisher full text, Methods, primary outcome and noninferiority plan; Results, Table 2 discussion; Discussion, limitations

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to six months in vaginal maturation index
results.note: Higher change with estrogen; adjusted P=0.02 after controlling for age, menopausal status, prior estrogen use, and sexual activity.
results.locator: Publisher full text, Results, paragraph discussing Table 2

harms.label: Reported adverse events
harms.locator: Publisher full text, Results, paragraph preceding Table 4; PubMed abstract, Conclusions
harms.note: Ten mild or moderate events across both groups included vaginal bleeding, pain or discharge, breast tenderness, urinary tract infection, migraine, and abdominal cramping. No serious adverse events were reported. Arm-specific counts appear only in an image table.

delivery.label: Eligibility threshold
delivery.value: At least 12 months without menstruation and bothersome vaginal dryness of at least 7 cm on a 10-cm VAS.
delivery.locator: Publisher full text, Methods, eligibility paragraph

delivery.label: Laser protocol
delivery.value: Three SmartXide2 V2LR/MonaLisa Touch intravaginal treatments at least six weeks apart; 30 W, 1,000 μs dwell, 1,000 μm spacing, smart stack 1 then 3; a 90° probe withdrawn by centimeters and rotated circumferentially; optional introital/vestibular treatment at 26 W.
delivery.locator: Publisher full text, Methods, Vaginal laser protocol

delivery.label: Estrogen protocol
delivery.value: Conjugated estrogen (Premarin) cream 0.5 g intravaginally daily for 14 days, then 0.5 g twice weekly for 24 weeks.
delivery.locator: Publisher full text, Methods, Vaginal estrogen protocol

delivery.label: Enrollment and completion
delivery.value: 196 planned; 69 enrolled; 62 completed six-month protocol; enrollment closed after the FDA required the sponsor to obtain and maintain an investigational device exemption.
delivery.locator: Publisher full text, Methods, power analysis; Results, opening paragraph

delivery.label: Treatment variation and aftercare
delivery.value: Optional vestibular treatment was given to 16 participants; 17 received vaginal treatment only. Intercourse was avoided for at least three days after each laser treatment; topical lidocaine 5% ointment was offered for vulvar pain.
delivery.locator: Publisher full text, Methods, Vaginal laser protocol; Results, treatment paragraph
